text:
Mathew Barzal made his season debut on Nov. 14 against Anaheim after a knee injury kept him out of the first month, and three games in, the Islanders look better with him. He has three assists, all in his first two games, both wins, and New York has taken 66% of the expected goals at five on five (the quality of chances) with him on the ice.

Three games is nothing, so treat every number here as a hint. His ice time, 16.6 minutes a night, is about four below last season, which is what you'd expect from a team easing a star back in.

What he brings is clear from last season. Evolving-Hockey had him 20th among 401 forwards in wins above replacement, and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him carrying the puck in on 66% of his entries and in the 96th percentile for primary shot assists. That's the skill the Islanders have missed. Stefen Rosner flagged him running a unit with Bo Horvat and Matthew Schaefer in overtime in Winnipeg, a trio worth watching.
headline: Barzal is back after a long wait
